actions: depresses/protracts the scapula, elevates ribs 3-5 (accessory inspiration when the scapula is fixed)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Deep to pectoralis major; the axillary artery and brachial plexus cords pass directly behind it. More precisely, the cords' names (lateral/medial/posterior) are defined by their position relative to the axillary artery's 2nd part -- which is itself the segment of the artery running directly posterior to this muscle, so 'relative to pectoralis minor' is the standard shorthand for a relationship that is technically defined one step removed, via the artery (adjusted for precision after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.notes: Three-quarters of muscle length. The needle path crosses toward the chest wall and the underlying brachial plexus, which is why the source treats ultrasound as mandatory here.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part II -- Proximal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(6):276 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17060276 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites (Yi, Li, Yang, Moon and others)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transducer angled 45 degrees toward the axilla on the anterior thoracic wall, along the midclavicular line, about 5-6 cm distal to the clavicle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to pectoralis major, superficial to the rib cortex and intercostal muscles.
structures_at_risk: brachial plexus and axillary vessels (the underlying neurovascular bundle)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Also injected for pectoralis minor syndrome, where the overactive muscle compresses the distal brachial plexus branches beneath it -- the same bundle that is the hazard of the injection.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part II -- Proximal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(6):276 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17060276 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites (Yi, Li, Yang, Moon and others)
